symbols.name: Simple Orienteering Course
symbols.description:
This symbol provides a simple and quick way to make training courses.

The purple line will extend a bit into the finish symbol. This is a shortcoming of this simple approach.

symbols.name: Start
symbols.description: The start or map issue point (if not at the start) is shown by an equilateral triangle which points in the direction of the first control. The centre of the triangle shows the precise position of the start point.

symbols.name: Control point
symbols.description: The control points are shown with circles. The centre of the circle shows the precise position of the feature. Sections of circles should be omitted to leave important detail showing.

symbols.name: Control number
symbols.description: The number of the control is placed close to the control point circle in such a way that it does not obscure important detail. The numbers are orientated to north.

symbols.name: Line
symbols.description: Where controls are to be visited in order, the start, control points and finish are joined together by straight lines. Sections of lines should be omitted to leave important detail showing.

symbols.name: Marked route
symbols.description: A marked route is shown on the map with a dashed line.

symbols.name: Finish
symbols.description: The finish is shown by two concentric circles.

symbols.name: Uncrossable boundary
symbols.description: A boundary which it is not permitted to cross.

symbols.name: Crossing point
symbols.description: A crossing point through or over a wall or fence, or across a road or railway or through a tunnel or an out-of-bounds area is drawn on the map with two lines curving outwards.

symbols.name: Out-of-bounds area
symbols.description:
An out-of-bounds area, see also symbol 528, is shown with vertical stripes.
A bounding line may be drawn if there is no natural boundary, as follows:
- a solid line indicates that the boundary is marked continuously (tapes, etc.) on the ground,
- a dashed line indicates intermittent marking on the ground,
- no line indicates no marking on the ground.

symbols.name: Out-of-bounds area, solid boundary
symbols.description: A solid line indicates that the boundary is marked continuously (tapes, etc.) on the ground.

symbols.name: Out-of-bounds area, dashed boundary
symbols.description: A dashed line indicates intermittent marking on the ground.

symbols.name: Dangerous area
symbols.description: An area presenting danger to the competitor is shown with cross-hatched diagonal lines.

symbols.name: Forbidden route
symbols.description: A route which is out-of-bounds is shown with crosses.

symbols.name: First aid post
symbols.description: The location of a first aid post.

symbols.name: Refreshment point
symbols.description: The location of a refreshment point which is not at a control.

symbols.name: Heading: Single line for event title or classes
symbols.description: Optionally this block can be used as [ Classes line ] between [ Event title ] and [ Course nature ].

symbols.name: Course nature
symbols.description:
This block describes the main parameters of a course. Its purpose is to help understand the degree of difficulty.
 - Scheme: | Course code | Length | Height climb |
 - The course length is given in kilometres rounded to the nearest 0.1 km.
 - The height climb is given in metres rounded to the nearest 5 m.

symbols.name: Description of individual control
symbols.description:
Scheme of columns: |A|B|C|D|E|F|G|H|

A: Control number
B: Control code
C: Which of any similar feature
D: Control feature
E: Appearance
F: Dimensions, combinations
G: Location of the control flag
H: Other information

symbols.name: Textual description of individual control
symbols.description:
Scheme of columns: |A|B|Text|

A: Control number
B: Control code

symbols.name: Thicker horizontal line
symbols.description:
A thicker horizontal line should be used after every third description and on either side of any special instruction.

In this symbol set, you need to add this symbol manually after the start location row and after every three consequent rows of 99.3 Description of individual control.

symbols.name: |A| Start location

symbols.name: |D| Earth bank

Map symbol: ISOM 308

symbols.name: |D| Open land

symbols.name: |D| Road

symbols.name: |D| Stairway

symbols.name: |D| Special item
symbols.description: If used, an explanation of its meaning must be supplied to competitors in the pre-race information.

symbols.name: |D| Special item
symbols.description: If used, an explanation of its meaning must be supplied to competitors in the pre-race information.

symbols.name: |D| Country Specific features (template)
symbols.description:
It is not generally recommended to introduce local symbols. If local symbols are used then at events likely to attract an international entry information about them should be supplied to competitors in the pre-race details.

The default line shows a box of 5 mm by 5mm and can be removed from the final symbols.

symbols.name: |E| Low
symbols.description: Where the control feature is particularly low or flat at but this is not indicated on the map; e.g. Hill, low.

symbols.name: |E| Shallow
symbols.description: Where the control feature is particularly shallow but this is not indicated on the map; e.g. Re-entrant, shallow.

symbols.name: |E| Deep

symbols.name: |E| Overgrown
symbols.description: Where the feature is partially covered in undergrowth or bushes that are not indicated on the map; e.g. Ruin, overgrown.

symbols.name: |E| Open
symbols.description: Where the feature is in an area where the tree cover is less than the surroundings but this is not indicated on the map; e.g. Marsh, open.

symbols.name: |E| Rocky, Stony
symbols.description: Where the feature is in an area of rocky or stony ground not indicated on the map; e.g. Pit, rocky.

symbols.name: |E| Marshy

symbols.name: |E| Sandy
symbols.description: Where the feature is in an area of sandy ground not indicated on the map; e.g. Spur, sandy.

symbols.name: |E| Needle leaved
symbols.description: Where the tree or trees associated with the control feature have needle shaped leaves; e.g. Distinctive tree, needle leaved.

symbols.name: |E| Broad leaved
symbols.description: Where the tree or trees associated with the control feature are broad-leaved; e.g. Copse, broad leaved.

symbols.name: |E| Ruined
symbols.description: Where the feature has fallen to ground level; e.g. Fence, ruined.

symbols.name: |F| Height or Depth
symbols.description: Height or Depth of the feature in metres; e.g. 2.6

symbols.name: |F| Size
symbols.description: Horizontal dimensions of the feature in metres; e.g. 8 x 4

symbols.name: |F| Slash for height on slope
symbols.description: Use with text symbol 9.4

symbols.name: |F| Heights of two features, or on slope
symbols.description:
Use this text symbol to give two numbers in different lines.

9.3 Height on slope: Height of the feature on a slope in metres.
Use the slash symbol 9.3 for separating the numbers; e.g.

0.5/
    / 3.0

9.4 Heights of two features: Heights of two features with the control between them. Write one number above the other; e.g.

2.0
3.0

symbols.name: |F| Crossing
symbols.description: The point at which two linear features cross. The two features which either cross or meet must be shown in columns |D| and |E|.

symbols.name: |F| Junction
symbols.description: The point at which two linear features meet. The two features which either cross or meet must be shown in columns |D| and |E|.

symbols.name: |G| North Corner (inside)
symbols.description:
Used where:
a) The edge of a feature turns through an angle of 45-135 degrees; e.g. Open land, east corner (inside).
b) A linear feature turns a corner; e.g. Fence, south corner (inside).
The orientation of the symbol indicates the direction in which the corner points.

a) The edge of a feature turns through an angle of 45-135 degrees; e.g. Ruin, north west corner (outside).
b) A linear feature turns a corner; e.g. Stone wall, south west corner (outside).
The orientation of the symbol indicates the direction in which the corner points.

symbols.name: |G| Upper Part
symbols.description: Where the feature extends over two or more contours and the control is located near the top; e.g. Erosion Gully, upper part.

symbols.name: |G| Lower Part
symbols.description: Where the feature extends over two or more contours and the control is located near the bottom; e.g. Re-entrant, lower part.

symbols.name: |G| Top
symbols.description: Where the control is located at the highest point of the feature and this is not the usual location; e.g. Cliff, top.

symbols.name: |G| Beneath
symbols.description: Where the control is located underneath the feature; e.g. Pipeline, beneath.

symbols.name: |G| Foot (no direction)
symbols.description: Where the control is located at the lower junction of the slope of the feature and the surface of the surrounding area; e.g. Earth bank, foot.

symbols.name: |G| North Foot
symbols.description: As above, but where the feature is large enough for the control to be placed in more than one location around it; e.g. Hill, north east foot.

symbols.name: |G| Between
symbols.description: Where the control is located between two features; e.g. Between thickets; Between boulder and knoll. The two features which the control is between must be shown separately in columns |D| and |E|.

symbols.name: |G| First aid post
symbols.description: Control site where First aid is available.

symbols.name: |G| Refreshment point
symbols.description: Control site where Refreshments are available.

symbols.name: |G| Radio or TV control
symbols.description: Location of a Radio or TV control.

symbols.name: |G| Control check
symbols.description: Manned control site where the control card is checked.

symbols.name: Taped Route, away from control
symbols.description: A marked route is to be followed away from a particular control. Re-emphasises what is shown on the map.

symbols.name: Taped Route, between controls
symbols.description: A marked route is to be followed between controls. Re-emphasises what is shown on the map.

symbols.name: Mandatory crossing point
symbols.description: Mandatory crossing points (or points) between two controls. Re-emphasises what is shown on the map.

symbols.name: Mandatory passage through out of bounds area
symbols.description: Mandatory route between two controls. Re-emphasises what is shown on the map.

symbols.name: Taped Route from Control to Map Exchange
symbols.description: At a map exchange, or if a marked route is to be followed from a control to a map exchange, this instruction follows the last control description of the first part of the course.

symbols.name: Taped Route from last control to Finish
symbols.description: Mandatory route from the last control to the Finish. Re-emphasises what is shown on the map. Gives the distance from the last control to Finish.

symbols.name: Taped Route from finish funnel to Finish
symbols.description: The competitor has to navigate from the last control to finish funnel, and then follow tapes. Gives the distance from the last control to Finish.

symbols.name: Navigation from last control to Finish (no Taped Route)
symbols.description: The competitor has to navigate from the last control to finish. No tapes. Gives the distance from the last control to Finish.

symbols.name: Length of special route
symbols.description: This is used with the special instruction (13.x) to give the distance from the last control to the end of the route (control, map exchange, or finish).
